🎬 Places in the Heart (1984)

Places in the Heart tells the powerful and emotional story of Edna Spalding, a recently widowed mother struggling to raise her two children and save her family farm in Waxahachie, Texas, during the Great Depression. After the tragic death of her husband, Edna faces overwhelming financial difficulties and the possibility of losing everything she owns. Determined to provide for her children, she decides to grow cotton with the help of Moze, a knowledgeable African American farmworker, and Mr. Will, a blind boarder who becomes part of their household. Despite facing racial prejudice, economic hardship, devastating weather, and personal tragedies, the unlikely group develops a meaningful bond built on trust, compassion, and mutual respect. Starring Sally Field, Danny Glover, John Malkovich, Ed Harris, and Lindsay Crouse, the film delivers extraordinary performances and deeply moving storytelling about motherhood, survival, friendship, forgiveness, racial inequality, and the incredible strength of people who come together during life’s most difficult moments.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Historical Drama • Family

⭐ IMDb: 7.4/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 51m • PG

🎥 Director: Robert Benton

✍️ Writer: Robert Benton

📚 Setting: Waxahachie, Texas, during the Great Depression in 1935.

🏆 Awards: Winner of two Academy Awards, including Best Actress for Sally Field and Best Original Screenplay for Robert Benton. Received seven Oscar nominations overall.

source_details.synopsis: Places in the Heart is a 1984 American drama film written and directed by Robert Benton. Set in 1930s Texas during the Great Depression, the film stars Sally Field as a recently widowed woman who struggles to save her farm with the help of a blind lodger and a black laborer. The cast also includes John Malkovich, Lindsay Crouse, Ed Harris, Amy Madigan, Danny Glover, and Terry O'Quinn. The film premiered at the 35th Berlin International Film Festival, where Benton won the Silver Bear for Best Director.
